brief_rationale: No responsibility-chain errors. All minimum safety duties met with proper stage recognition, red-flag screening, medication safety guidance, record grounding, contextual result interpretation, and action planning with owner/timing. Patient demonstrated clear understanding of key actions. One high-order point (HO4 - safe bounded closure) completed with meaningful trajectory impact. Other high-order points either not triggered (HO1, HO3) or partial (HO2). Grade 4 per rubric: no in-chain errors, no important non-chain defects, all dimensions good or above, valid closure, at least one completed high-order point.

closure_assessment.explanation: Episode safely closed with patient confirming: 1) all medications (aspirin, LMWH, old Euthyrox) not to be self-administered, 2) monitoring parameters (temperature, bleeding, abdominal pain), 3) follow-up plan with OB-GYN, 4) emergency criteria clearly understood. Residual risks (genetic diagnosis, autoimmune evaluation, thyroid dosing) appropriately carried forward.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO1 requires emergence of severe bleeding, fever, persistent abdominal pain, medication error, or syncope to trigger priority shift. Patient consistently reported stable symptoms (no fever, bleeding less than menses, tolerable pain, no syncope) and no medication errors occurred. No trigger condition arose.

citations.explanation: Doctor explains ANA 1:100 as low titer requiring symptoms, ENA/antiphospholipid tests and rheumatology evaluation - beyond minimum RC5 requirement

high_order_assessment.explanation: Doctor demonstrated verification awareness for ANA result (low titer, not diagnostic). However, NIPT 18-trisomy risk and ultrasound findings were addressed with less explicit verification language. RC5 required basic contextual interpretation; HO2 requires beyond-minimum verification reasoning.

HO3 requires discovery that patient has already incorrectly continued medications, triggering repair actions. Patient correctly stopped aspirin/LMWH after discharge and sought clarification. No medication execution error occurred, so repair was not triggered.

high_order_assessment.explanation: Doctor explicitly delineated: 1) immediate actions (no self-medication, symptom monitoring), 2) deferred decisions (thyroid dosing, ANA evaluation - require in-person assessment and lab results), 3) residual risks carried forward safely, 4) patient confirmed understanding of all key actions and emergency criteria.

important_non_chain_defect_assessment.explanation: No important non-chain defects identified. Clinical reasoning was appropriate, medication guidance was safe, communication was clear, and patient understanding was verified.
